title: Cache Engineering for Agents
summary: It replaces context-engineering approaches (trimming or summarizing history, which invalidates the prefix and forces re-prefill) with direct KV cache operations, drop and repos, that control active cache without altering the trajectory. The cost is operational: you must run or integrate the AKV serving engine to manage stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration, which excludes third-party API-only deployments and adds a serving-layer dependency. Failure modes include incorrect cache reuse from history dependence (identical token sequences with different cache states), potential accuracy loss if aggressive drop policies remove needed context, and policy fragility since gains depend on the workload-specific drop policy.
rationale: The cost and latency gains are quantified and relevant to agent workloads on a single 24 GB GPU, but adoption requires self-hosting a modified serving engine and validating the drop policy on the reader's own trajectories, so pilot testing rather than immediate adoption is warranted.
technique: Direct KV cache drop and reposition operations for agents

The cost is operational: you must run or integrate the AKV serving engine to manage stateful cache reuse, eviction, and restoration, which excludes third-party API-only deployments and adds a serving-layer dependency. Failure modes include incorrect cache reuse from history dependence (identical token sequences with different cache states), potential accuracy loss if aggressive drop policies remove needed context, and policy fragility since gains depend on the workload-specific drop policy.

Rolling-drop cache policy reduces average cost by 27.7% versus threshold-triggered summarization while improving benchmark scores by 1.7 points; the AKV engine adds up to 1.2x output throughput and 1.5x P95 latency speedup.
